title: Babylon falls to the Medes and Persians
summary: Babylon falls to the Medes and Persians
description: Added from the Generations curriculum import (Preparing the World for Jesus (1st ed., 2020)). Jones, Appendix F (23rd ed., 2026), sets the sort. The Generations dates below stay on display.

sorting_basis.note: Tier 3: Ussher-Jones (Floyd Nolen Jones): 539 BC (no higher-tier year available).

chronologies.note: pending CFAH reference (the CFAH series does not cover this period; no tier 1–4 date exists)

chronologies.date: 3465 539 Babylon falls to Darius the Mede
chronologies.citation: Jones, The Chronology of the Old Testament: A Return to the Basics, 23rd ed. (Master Books, 2026), Appendix F, printed p. 280 (PDF p. 315)
chronologies.note: Jones names Darius the Mede as the one to whom Babylon falls.

chronologies.citation: Preparing the World for Jesus (1st ed., 2020), ch. 11 "Babylon Has Fallen (626–539 BC)", PDF p. 343 (printed p. 342)
chronologies.note: Also p. 345 and the Timeline Reviews (pp. 354, 388).
chronologies.edition_note: 1st ed. (2020); superseded by the 2nd ed. (2024), which prints "539 BC" (PDF p. 497): the same date.

chronologies.citation: Preparing the World for Jesus (2nd ed., 2024), ch. 19 "Babylon Has Fallen", PDF p. 497 (printed p. 483)
chronologies.note: Belshazzar is co-regent (no year printed for his appointment).

chronologies.date: 539, B.C. (OCR misread "5939"; the page image reads 539)
chronologies.citation: Morecraft, A Christian Survey of World History, p. 27 (PDF p. 35)
chronologies.note: The Medes and Persians under Cyrus take Babylon. Compare PDF pp. 51–52, which end the Babylonian empire in 536 B.C.

chronologies.citation: Morecraft, A Christian Survey of World History, p. 44 (PDF p. 52)
chronologies.note: From the book's "Ancient Empires" pages (credited in an image to Daily Bible Study, keyway.ca). The Babylonian empire "came to an end when it fell to the Persians". Internal: PDF p. 35 gives 539 B.C. for the same conquest.

chronologies.date: “with the first approach of the ensuing spring, marched forward against Babylon”
chronologies.citation: Herodotus, Histories 1.190 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 84 (PDF p. 86)
chronologies.note: Cyrus lost a whole summer at the Gyndes and marched on Babylon the next spring.

chronologies.date: “Such, then, were the circumstances of the first taking of Babylon.”
chronologies.citation: Herodotus, Histories 1.191 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 85 (PDF p. 87)
chronologies.note: Cyrus takes Babylon by diverting the Euphrates; the "second" taking is by Darius (3.159). Herodotus gives no year; Generations dates it 539 BC (provisional).

chronologies.date: takes Babylon, first of his sovereignty 536
chronologies.citation: Hales, A New Analysis of Chronology and Geography, History and Prophecy, 2nd ed., corrected and improved (London: C. J. G. & F. Rivington, 1830), vol. II, Synopsis of the Chronology, p. xxxvi
